claims.text: The proposed intervention is 50% cold rolling followed by annealing at 900°C for 10 minutes under an inert atmosphere.
Cold rolling followed by moderate annealing will produce a fine-grained microstructure.
The treatment will produce a dual-phase microstructure.
The treated microstructure will have increased grain-boundary density and uniformly distributed fine recrystallized grains.
Minor ductile precipitates may form at grain boundaries.
Cold rolling induces substantial deformation that enables subsequent microstructural refinement.
The 900°C anneal promotes controlled recrystallization after cold rolling.
Fine grains and localized ductile phases at grain boundaries distribute plastic strain more uniformly.
Increased grain-boundary density improves ductility by delaying crack nucleation.
Strength derived from the refractory elements remains largely preserved after treatment.
The treated alloy will exhibit more uniform deformation than the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy will have at least approximately 30% greater strain-to-failure than the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will reduce yield strength by less than 5% relative to the as-cast baseline.
Impact-induced energy release will be maintained after treatment.
As-cast refractory high-entropy alloys have coarse-grained, relatively homogeneous, brittle microstructures.
Untreated coarse-grained samples have lower ductility and a greater propensity for strain localization while retaining high strength and energy-release characteristics.
The expected benefits apply at ambient temperature under both quasi-static tensile and high-strain-rate impact loading.
Substantially higher annealing temperatures may cause excessive grain growth and negate the improvement.
